ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: A city of a hundred thousand people, planned on a grid, that shaped Mesoamerica centuries before the Aztecs.
The last and greatest power of Mesoamerica: tribute, war and a capital on a lake.
The island metropolis that stunned the Spaniards, larger than most cities of Europe.
The emperor who received Cortes, and whose fate still divides historians.
The largest state of the pre-Columbian Americas, run by roads, storehouses and knotted cords instead of writing.
The royal estate in the clouds that conquest never found.
The Inca who won a civil war just in time to meet Pizarro at Cajamarca.
